ev: Morongo Indian reservation had extensive mud, rock and logs in a major debris flow off the 2020 Apple burn scar which traveled down the San Gorgonio River. This inundated the Banning Water Plant and pushed mud, rocks and logs onto roads.

A storm survey by WCM found several debris flows on Valley of the Falls road in Forest Falls. The largest produced mud and rocks as high as 10 feet, completely covering the Valley of the Falls road. Other flash floods and debris occurred further into the canyon (deeper) affecting the roads and residences property. Homeowners discussed and described the flooding and impact. Most severe since August 2014.

A major flash flood debris flow occurred in Birch Creek through Potato Canyon. This area was affected by lesser debris flows October and December 2021 and August 2022 but this flood filled the entire channel in layers, overtopped and damage the Steakhouse restaurant in Oak Glen, took out power poles, pushed large boulder and layers of mud downstream onto Oak Glen Road and pushed up to windows on a couple homes. WCM Alex Tardy did a storm survey. Estimated 100,000 cubic yards of debris removed by San Bernardino Public Works. Video of the debris flow between 3 and 4 pm was recorded.

A large flash flood and debris flow occurred on Prospect street off of Valley of the Falls in Forest Falls, CA. The debris flow originated on the 2020 El Dorado burn scar after 1.1 inches of rain in an hour on Yucaipa Ridge. More than 1 debris flow occurred but the largest crossed Prospect street moving and damaging vehicles as well as damage homes. At least 2 homes had major damage. One fatality occurred when an older female was buried in debris, 3 days later found by search and rescue dogs. Residents took photos of debris flows and flash flooding including video and Ring security cameras. WCM visited the damage and SAR activity on September 13 and spoke with residents who shared additional photos and descriptions. A 20 foot boulder was lodged just above their home and their Jeep was washed down the hill (caught on Ring camera).
